items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: As a matter when Billy Exstine was putting together that band, almost everybody out of his first band that wasn‟t with Earl Hines came out of Tommy Miles‟ band because he used to sing with the band.

ctx.x: As a matter when Billy Exstine was putting together that band, almost everybody out of his first band that wasn‟t with Earl Hines came out of Tommy Miles‟ band because he used to sing with the band.

Sure. Yeah, that was really a spoiling grounds. They had these territorial bands out of Cincinnati and out of Washington, D.C. There was one out of Baltimore. I remember a band out of Baltimore. Scat Man Caruthers was a drummer in one of those bands, one of those territory bands out of Cincinnati. I remember him when he was playing drums in one of the bands. Stayed at Uncle Henry‟s [laughter]

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: one of my best pictures is a picture of you, Lou Rawls, and Billy Eckstine trading choruses on the blues

ctx.x: Oh, yeah but you were shocked, Tom Whaley. Tom said, “You want me to conduct?” I said, “You made the arrangements, why don’t you conduct it?” Oh, man.

Well I’ve been a lucky dude, because I talk like my sister, Pearl Bailey always says, “I’ve been to the White House so many times I just call it ‘The House.’” So I’ve been in there, and everybody knew me pretty well, and I always had a camera, and everybody was looking at me going around with the cameras you know. So when jam sessions got to be going, I handed somebody else the bass, and I had my camera and I went around, and I really took some pictures. I took some pictures that I really love. I’ve got pictures…
Of Duke Ellington dancing with Carmen deLavallade. I have it on my wall at home.
